EIT Tairāwhiti | We're Local, Like You

From the classroom to the surf, Tairāwhiti offers the ultimate study-to-play lifestyle. If you’re into surfing, fishing, diving, and hunting our Tairāwhiti campus might be the perfect fit for you!

If you’re dreaming of a study journey where you can stay connected to the coast, the bush, and your community, EIT Tairāwhiti has the space, and the vibe, to help you thrive.

Kelsey Goldsmith and Graeme Card | EIT Te Reo Māori Graduates

From study to stronger community connections, Te Reo Māori is shaping careers at Gisborne District Council.

We’re proud to share this kōrero from Kelsey Goldsmith and Graeme Card, two EIT Te Reo Māori graduates who are now using their learning every day in their roles at Gisborne District Council.

As a policy planner, Kelsey explains how essential tikanga and te reo are in her mahi, guiding the way she engages with people and places across the region. Graeme, who works in an outward facing role with iwi and hapū, shares how learning te reo and understanding tikanga has deepened his ability to connect, communicate, and work respectfully with the community.
Both Kelsey and Graeme say their EIT courses have been invaluable in growing their confidence, their capability, and their careers.

If you’re working alongside iwi, hapū, or community groups, or want to strengthen your personal understanding of te ao Māori, take the next steps in your study journey with EIT Tairāwhiti, we’re local, like you.

Tracey Tangihaere | EIT Tairāwhiti Executive Director

From classroom learning to coastal living, experience what makes Tairāwhiti unique.

In this kōrero, Tracey Tangihaere, Executive Director of EIT’s Tairāwhiti Campus, takes us to beautiful Waikanae Beach, just minutes from where students learn, study, and connect.

Tracey shares one of the best parts about studying in Tairāwhiti: the ability to step out between classes, head to the beach for lunch, bring your surfboard and your togs, and enjoy everything this stunning region has to offer. It’s a place where education and lifestyle blend seamlessly, creating a study experience that’s relaxed, supportive, and uniquely Gisborne.

If you’re dreaming of learning in a close knit community with sunshine, surf, and a campus right on the doorstep of the ocean, EIT Tairāwhiti might just be the perfect place to begin your journey.

Joe Alexander | EIT Bachelor of Computing Systems Graduate

From classroom projects to motion capture TV production, follow along Joe Alexander’s journey into the world of screen arts and intelligent systems.
We’re excited to share this kōrero from Bachelor of Computing Systems graduate, Joe Alexander, as he reflects on his internship at Rāngai Film School.

Joe talks about one of his first big tasks, setting up motion capture technology for the team and how his focus in intelligent systems, robotics, and AI prepared him to step confidently into a creative, fast paced industry.
Rāngai Managing Director, Shannon Dowsing, shares how impressed he’s been with Joe’s skills, adaptability, and ability to work across both IT and screen arts. What started as an internship has now led to Joe working on a TV show, proving just how much opportunity sits at the intersection of tech and creativity.

If you’re someone who loves problem solving, innovation, and using technology to bring ideas to life, Joe’s journey is an inspiring example of where a Bachelor of Computing Systems can take you and how far your curiosity can go.

Blaze and Joe | EIT Exercise Level 4 Graduates

From classroom learning to real‑world coaching — building confident leaders in the exercise industry .
 
We're excited to share this kōrero with Blaze Stafford and Joe Tangira, two proud graduates of the NZ Certificate in Exercise (Level 4) who are now out in the community helping others move, grow, and thrive.

In this video, Blaze and Joe talk about what inspired them to study exercise, the hands‑on learning that shaped their skills, and how the programme gave them the confidence to step into roles where they can genuinely make a difference. Their passion for health, fitness, and supporting people shines through every moment.

If you’re someone who loves being active, working with people, and creating positive change, their journey is an awesome example of where this qualification can take you.

Facebook live: A water Safety discussion

Are you a keen boatie or maritime enthusiast? Tune in to our Facebook Live discussion and hear directly from our Harbourmaster.

Facebook live: Council's Strategic Priorities

Hawke’s Bay Regional Council Chair Sophie Siers and Deputy Chair Jerf van Beek unpack the key priorities guiding the Regional Council’s work.

They will discuss how we are working to reduce flood risk, improve water security, maintain land and water health, address changing climate, financial health and affordability.

This is an opportunity to ask questions about these priorities and hear how they influence the work of the Regional Council and build regional resilience.

Drury Rail Stations test train

Our Drury Rail Stations caught a glimpse of the future on Monday, with test trains stopping at each platform for the first time to check clearances.
 
More test trains have been running across Auckland yesterday and today as we work alongside Auckland Transport, City Rail Link and Auckland One Rail to trial the new high frequency City Rail Link timetable which will start later this year.

KiwiRail Auckland summer rail upgrades

Today is a major milestone for Auckland’s rail network - trains are back up and running after a successful summer rail upgrade and CRL timetable testing.
 
Also - the Rail Network Rebuild is finished! A  huge leap forward in the lead up to the City Rail Link opening later this year.
 
Thank you to our customers and Aucklanders for their patience and support as we improved our network to support more frequent trains.
 
Check out our highlights in this video.

Track maintenance: tamping

When we upgrade rail infrastructure, one of the final steps in the process is tamping. Tamping also plays an important role as an ongoing maintenance activity. The tamper machine adjusts the track alignment by lifting the rails and compacting the ballast underneath, helping to keep the track stable and in the right place.   
 
Watch this video to hear Project Engineer Sebastian Allum explain why tamping is crucial for reducing track faults and the number of Temporary Speed Restrictions, supporting a more reliable rail network for both passenger and freight services.

Wellington summer works wrap up

The Wellington rail network reopened last week, allowing us to continue serving passengers and customers.

Following a successful summer works closure, we’re proud to share some of our favourite highlights.

A huge thank you to Wellingtonians for your patience, and to our teams who gave up their holidays to help deliver a better rail network.

12th International Interoperability Testing Event | Wellington NZ 2025

The Department of Internal Affairs and NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi co-hosted the 12th International Interoperability Test Event for Digital Standards. The event brought together public and private sector digital leaders from New Zealand and around the world to test how digital credential systems work together.

PCE Estimate of environmental expenditure 2025/26 - NZ Parliament Environment Committee

The Parliamentary Commissioner for the Environment, Simon Upton and staff present the fifth annual Estimate of Environmental Expenditure. The PCE monitors how public funds are used for environmental outcomes and reports their findings to Parliament via the Environment Select Committee. 
Read the report here: https://pce.parliament.nz/publications/estimate-of-environmental-expenditure-202526-method-and-results/

We Are Not Your Dusky Maidens – Phylesha Brown Acton

Watch Phylesha Brown-Acton talk about how adornment influences her life as a Niuean woman, and the Western trope of Pacific women being perceived and portrayed as anonymous exotic dusky maidens.

The subtitles are available in English, te reo Māori and Niuean. As YouTube doesn't have the Niuean language listed, the Niuean subtitles are listed as Tongan.

We Are Not Your Dusky Maidens! – Mata Atonio

Watch Mata Atonio talk about how adornment influences her life as a Sāmoan woman, and finding out the names of some of the women photographed in Sāmoa who remain unnamed.

Thames-Coromandel Mayoral Disaster Relief Fund Opens

The Mayoral Disaster Relief Fund is open to Thames-Coromandel District Council residents, ratepayers or small business owners, and not-for-profit organisations who have suffered financial hardship because of damages caused by the weather event. 

The Fund may be used to support and meet the needs of affected individuals, families, community organisations, small businesses and marae. 

See our website for more: https://www.tcdc.govt.nz/relief

The digital screen sector is rapidly growing, in areas such as virtual production, 3D storytelling, virtual and augmented reality, and more. UC's new international-quality workspaces, stages, studios, and more — provides a space for film production, game development, and cross-reality technologies to come together.

Update on Civil Defence work in Whangarei District

Here’s an update from Mayor Ken Couper, Civil Defence Controller Victoria Harwood, Rōpata Diamond of the Ngātiwai Trust Board and NRC Chair Pita Tipene on today’s outreach to affected communities.  

We hosted a visit by Prime Minister Luxon, who was accompanied by Minister of Emergency Management and Recovery Mark Mitchell, and our local MPs. This was an opportunity for them to see the extent of the impact of this week’s storm events and discuss recovery efforts. 

Mayor Couper also acknowledged the tragic news announced this afternoon from Tauranga, passing on aroha to the families and response agencies involved in the search and recovery efforts.  

For more information on our response efforts:  
https://www.wdc.govt.nz/Community/Civil-Defence/Latest-updates
